record_type_quote: Because this might reflect inadequate statistical power, we undertook two replication attempts of the behavioral paradigm, failing both times to observe more forgetting for competitors than targets.

targets.authors: Wimber, M., Alink, A., Charest, I., Kriegeskorte, N., & Anderson, M. C.
targets.title: Retrieval induces adaptive forgetting of competing memories via cortical pattern suppression.
targets.evidence_quote: For this reason, we sought to replicate the behavioral results from this paradigm.
targets.outcome_quote: Across multiple replication attempts, we failed to replicate the finding of forgetting for competitors reported by Wimber et al. for their behavioral results.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall failure verdict applies to the central forgetting effect despite successful learning during selective retrieval. Original data are also reanalyzed; this does not turn the new-sample attempts into reproductions.

reasoning: Matching title, DOI, and three authors verified in complete primary article (20 pages including references). New participant samples make the record a replication. One original paper is directly retested; the inhibition theory papers and other RIF studies are background. Attempts 2 and 3 are reported in the main paper; initial attempt 1 is described but principally relegated to supplement. Original-data robustness component recorded separately.

original_data_reanalysis.outcome_computational_quote: We report the significance of the interaction between associate type and condition for the original data in which missing data was labeled to be errors, versus the original data in which missing data is excluded from the analyses.
original_data_reanalysis.computation_evidence_note: Table 1 reproduces original ANOVA interaction p=.041 with missing responses coded as errors.
original_data_reanalysis.outcome_robustness_quote: Critically, though, if one trims out the missing data, the interaction is not significant regardless of the statistical test.
